previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a long history of recurrent pancreatitis was readmitted due to a flare triggered by attempting to eat solid food shortly after a prior discharge. She presented with severe epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control using a Dilaudid PCA initially, then transitioned to oral hydromorphone. TPN was initiated for nutritional support. An endoscopic ultrasound showed no pancreatic mass, and MRCP revealed only chronic changes. A non-occlusive thrombus was detected near the left PICC line, prompting its removal and placement of a new PICC in the right arm. Estrogen therapy with Premarin was discontinued due to thrombosis risk. She improved clinically, with pain control and tolerance of oral medications, and was discharged home with visiting nurse support for PICC and TPN management, along with follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
#Acute on chronic pancreatitis - CT of the abdomen and pelvis 
did not reveal any pancreatic abnormality such as pseudocyst. 
The patient was treated with bowel rest, IVF, TPN, antiemetics, 
and narcotic analgesics. Her pain improved significantly with 
the addition of a fentanyl patch. She was able to tolerate a 
clear diet prior to discharge. She will continue on TPN via a 
___ catheter as an outpatient and will have chemistries 
checked weekly to adjust the TPN formulation accordingly.    
.
#Nosocomial PNA - The patient developed low-grade fevers and a 
CXR revealed a right mid-lung and basilar opacity, suggestive of 
pneumonia. As she had been in the hospital for 10 days and had 
recently undergone EGD with conscious sedation, she was started 
on antibiotic coverage for nosocomial and aspiration pneumonia. 
She was encouraged to use incentive spirometry. She will 
complete a 7-day course of antibiotics as an outpatient. 
.  
#Anemia - There were no signs or symptoms of acute bleeding. 
Iron studies were consistent with iron deficiency and anemia of 
chronic inflammation. She was guaiac negative. She underwent EGD 
on ___ which revealed linear erythema in the gastric antrum 
(the pathology from which showed chronic inactive gastritis with 
focal intestinal metaplasia but no dysplasia) and normal 
duodenal mucosa. She was transfused 1 U PRBC on ___ for Hct 
23.9. She will have her Hct checked by ___ 2 days after 
discharge and if <25% will have a repeat Hct checked within 48 
hours. She was instructed to call her physician or return to the 
Emergency Department if Hct <21%. It was strongly encouraged 
that the patient have a colonoscopy as soon as possible as she 
has never had one.
.  
#Pancytopenia - This appeared to be a chronic, stable process 
most likely due to marrow suppression in the setting of chronic 
inflammation. She was seen in consultation by 
hematology/oncology who did not feel that a bone marrow biopsy 
was indicated and recommended further evaluation as an 
outpatient.
.  
#Eosinophilia - This is a chronic issue of unclear etiology but 
the absolute eosinophil count has never exceeded 1000. There 
were no clear offending medications or strong history of atopy. 
Serum IgE was low-normal. Stool O&P were negative x 3. Pathology 
from the EGD on ___ showed chronic inactive gastritis with 
focal intestinal metaplasia but no dysplasia, as above.
.  
#Depression - Continued wellbutrin, zoloft, trazodone.  
.  
#GERD - Continued PPI therapy.
.  
#Nutrition - TPN, clear diet
.
#Prophylaxis - Subcutaneous heparin, PPI, bowel regimen.
